strengths: Meets every spec point. There are 4 pages with a shared nav and aria-current, and 14 books across 6 genres with a radio-group filter kept in ?genre=. pushState and popstate are handled, unknown or hostile values fall back to All, and the 'Showing N of 14' count is a live region.

The accessibility work is solid: a skip link that moves focus into main, a fieldset and legend for the filter, a visible :focus-visible ring, correct heading levels, and a semantic hours table with row headers. Contact form errors use aria-invalid and aria-describedby and focus the first invalid field. Touch targets are 44px.
Event upcoming/past splitting and the today/open status use the local date rather than UTC, and empty states are handled on both the events and home pages.
The JS is small and idiomatic: IIFE modules share a pure data/helper module, and all DOM is built with textContent, so there is no injection risk.

There are 57 Playwright tests that drive real headless Chrome. They cover filter history, hostile inputs, timezone edge cases, contrast, overflow at 360px, network isolation and form validation, and all 57 pass.
The copy is warm and consistent: 'six genres' matches the data, the staff picks link to the filtered catalogue, and the README covers running the site, running the tests, and where content lives.
reports.summary: Build I is a polished, accessible, spec-complete bookshop site in plain HTML, CSS and JS. Its genre filter is URL-backed, keyboard-operable and announces its result count. The contact form validation is accessible, and dates and hours are worked out from local time. A thorough Playwright suite (57 tests) passes cleanly. The only defects are minor: the two columns on the visit page are out of line because of a global section margin rule, one line of copy contradicts the address, the hours caption repeats the heading, the status message doesn't say when the shop next opens, and the design is text-only.

defects.what: Event data is hard-coded with dates ending 2027-01-16. After that date the events page and the home page show only the empty-state message, so the site goes stale without anyone noticing. The data-sufficiency test avoids this by fixing the clock at 2026-11-16.
defects.evidence: js/events.js: the last entry has date "2027-01-16". tests/site.test.js:521-527 use new Date(2026, 10, 16, 9).

defects.what: upcomingEvents compares dates only. An event earlier today still shows as upcoming after its start time has passed (for example, a 10:00 storytime still listed at 21:00 the same day).
defects.evidence: js/events.js upcomingEvents: filter is `event.date >= today`. Time is used only for sorting.

defects.what: The over-2000-character message check cannot trigger through normal input because the textarea already has maxlength=2000. The check and its test only cover values set from script.
defects.evidence: visit.html:192 maxlength="2000"; js/visit.js:44 `field.value.length > MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH`

defects.what: Opening hours are written out twice by hand: once as prose on the home page and once in the table on the visit page. Unlike books and events, they have no single source, so the two copies can drift apart.
defects.evidence: index.html 'Opening hours' section prose vs visit.html hours-table

defects.what: The tests rely on a globally installed Playwright and a fixed Chrome path (/usr/bin/google-chrome), and `npm test` fails unless NODE_PATH is set by hand. The README says this, but the test setup is not portable.
defects.evidence: README.md 'Running the tests' section; package.json has no devDependencies

defects.what: The book filter's role=status region is filled on page load, so some screen readers announce 'Showing all 15 books' unprompted. The message counter also updates silently, which is acceptable.

strengths: Meets every spec requirement: four pages share one nav with aria-current; index.html is at the root; no external requests; and the 360px layout is verified in screenshots and by tests, including at 200% text size.

The genre filter is well built: a native radio fieldset with a legend and a count per genre, URL state through pushState with working Back/popstate, unknown genres fall back to All, non-canonical genres are rewritten with replaceState, and the result count goes to a status region.

Solid accessibility: skip link, a programmatically focusable main, visible focus styles with a separate colour on dark backgrounds, 44px targets, a menu toggle with aria-expanded where Escape closes it and returns focus, a properly structured hours table, and logical heading order.

A careful contact form: novalidate with JS checks, per-field errors linked through aria-describedby, aria-invalid, an error summary in an alert region, focus moved to the first invalid field, whitespace-only input rejected, an honest 'demo, not sent' message with a mailto fallback, and the message replaced rather than duplicated on resubmit.
Book and event data each live in one place and are rendered with DOM APIs using textContent (no innerHTML). The code is small, readable IIFE modules.

Rich, consistent content: 15 books with blurbs and prices across 5 genres, 7 events with admission details, and directions by bus, car and bike. The covers are tasteful CSS-only placeholders marked aria-hidden.

Strong test suite: 50 headless-Chrome tests that all pass, covering console errors, off-origin requests, headings and landmarks, 360px overflow, filter and URL state, Back, event date edge cases and form validation.
reports.summary: Build J is a polished, spec-complete static bookshop site: 4 pages, 15 books with a URL-backed accessible genre filter, data-driven events, and a well-validated demo contact form. It looks good at both 1280px and 360px. In the copy at /tmp/inspect-website-bookshop-J, all 50 headless-Chrome tests passed (NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g) node --test tests/*.test.js). The only defects are minor: hard-coded event dates that will go stale after January 2027, a date-only check for upcoming events, a dead over-length check behind maxlength, hours written out twice by hand, and a test setup that depends on a global Playwright and a fixed Chrome path. A solid production-quality small project.
